title: How to Greet People at Work

sentences: Q:Dear Max, At the start of virtual meetings, should I say hello to everyone?
It seems to absorb a lot of time, but I don't want to be unfriendly.
translations: 问：亲爱的Max，在虚拟会议开始时，我应该向每个人打招呼吗？
这似乎很耗时，但我不想显得不友好。

sentences: Virtual calls put the hell in hello.
Every greeting prompts other participants to spend ages unmuting before saying "hello" back.
Some people then ask "how is everyone?", forcing everyone to unmute again and say something wildly insightful like "fine".
By the time that's over, someone else has joined the call and the whole cycle starts again.
Use the rule of three.
If there are three or more other people already on the line, just wave.
translations: 虚拟通话让“你好”变成了“你好烦”。
每次问候都促使其他参与者花很长时间取消静音，然后才回复“你好”。
接着有人问“大家怎么样？”，迫使所有人再次取消静音，说些像“挺好的”这样毫无新意的话。
等这一轮结束，又有其他人加入了通话，整个循环又开始了。
运用“三人法则”。
如果线上已经有三个或更多其他人，只需挥手示意即可。

sentences: Q:I am a germophobe and hate shaking hands with people.
I pine for the days of the pandemic, when no one touched each other at all.
What do you advise?
translations: 问：我有洁癖，讨厌和别人握手。
我怀念疫情期间的日子，那时人们完全不互相接触。
你有什么建议？

sentences: Your best bet is to wear a mask: there's no more cost-effective way to get people to keep their hands to themselves.
You could also ask your employer if you could work from home, or from an iron lung.
If that is a step too far, you could do that pandemic-era thing of extending the point of your elbow towards people, and hope they will reciprocate.
But what made some sense then looks weird now: like you don't know what those things at the end of your arms are for, or have been in a coma for five years.
translations: 你最好的选择是戴口罩：没有比这更具成本效益的方式让人们管好自己的手了。
你也可以问问雇主能否在家工作，或者用铁肺工作。
如果那太过分了，你可以做那种疫情时代的事——向人们伸出你的肘尖，并希望他们也会这样做。
但当时有些道理的事情现在看起来很奇怪：好像你不知道你手臂末端那些东西是干什么用的，或者你已经昏迷了五年。

sentences: Q:I suffer from anxiety over how to greet people, particularly those I know a bit but not well.
I spent some time in Japan in my youth, and to avoid deciding whether to hug someone or not, I stop before I get within touching distance and bow.
It's amazing how often people will bow back.
Is this a sensible strategy?
translations: 问：我对于如何问候他人感到焦虑，尤其是那些我有点认识但不太熟的人。
我年轻时在日本待过一段时间，为了避免决定是否要拥抱某人，我会在进入可触碰距离之前停下来并鞠躬。
令人惊讶的是，人们常常会回礼鞠躬。
这是一个明智的策略吗？

sentences: It depends a bit on whether you are still in Japan.
But the pre-emptive greeting is a good tactic wherever you are.
Another variant of this approach is to do a lot of performative stuff as you get close to someone: saying hello loudly, waving madly and smiling like an idiot.
Stop about two metres short of the other person, well out of range, and if necessary keep waving and saying hello for a bit.
If you are in a meeting room, move quickly to the other side of the table as you wave.
If you appear to be unhinged but extremely friendly, you will have hit the right mark.
No other greeting will be needed.
translations: 这在一定程度上取决于你是否还在日本。
但无论你在哪里，先发制人的问候都是一个好策略。
这种方法的另一种变体是，当你接近某人时，做很多表演性的事情：大声打招呼、疯狂挥手、像傻瓜一样微笑。
在距离对方大约两米处停下，远远超出接触范围，如有必要，继续挥手并打招呼一会儿。
如果你在会议室里，挥手时迅速移动到桌子的另一边。
如果你看起来有点疯狂但极其友好，那你就做对了。
不需要其他问候了。

sentences: Q:I don't know how to greet female colleagues I have worked with for years.
I could shake hands with them, as I do with other men, but it seems a little formal.
Do you have any advice?
translations: 问：我不知道该如何问候共事多年的女同事。
我可以像对待其他男同事一样和她们握手，但这似乎有点正式。
你有什么建议吗？

sentences: This question is one of the ones I get most often, at least from people in America and western Europe.
The classic advice is to shake hands with everyone, regardless of how well you know them.
It works as a greeting between men, so should work as a greeting between sexes, too.
If you want to add a bit of familiarity, use both hands to project extra warmth.
translations: 这个问题是我最常被问到的之一，至少来自美国和西欧的人是这样。
经典的建议是与每个人握手，无论你与他们熟悉程度如何。
这作为男性之间的问候方式有效，因此也应该适用于不同性别之间的问候。
如果你想增加一点亲切感，可以用双手握手以传递额外的温暖。

sentences: But there are times when handshaking feels genuinely awkward: when you see a close colleague socially, for example.
My advice in these circumstances is never to be the first mover: wait and see what the other person does and match them.
The risk is that you sacrifice some agency, and end up in an unwanted clinch.
But at least you didn't start it.
translations: 但有时握手确实会让人感到尴尬：例如，当你在社交场合遇到一位关系密切的同事时。
在这种情况下，我的建议是永远不要做第一个主动的人：先观察对方怎么做，然后配合他们。
风险在于你会失去一些主动权，最终陷入一个不想要的拥抱。
但至少不是你开始的。

sentences: Q:I was recently involved in an unfortunate hugging incident at work.
I got my timing and targeting all wrong, and ended up with the other person's ear lobe in my mouth.
Where did I go wrong, and what should I have done?
translations: 问：我最近在工作中卷入了一起不幸的拥抱事件。
我的时机和瞄准完全搞错了，结果把对方的耳垂含在了嘴里。
我错在哪里，又应该怎么做？

sentences: If you do end up at close quarters, remember that an embrace at work is not meant to be an actual embrace, just a faint echo of one.
If you are hugging someone, behave as though you are playing that children's game called "Operation".
Put your arm around the other person without actually touching any part of their body.
Keep your face well away from theirs: unless they have unusually big ear lobes, you should never find yourself in that kind of horrendous situation again.
translations: 如果你真的近距离接触，记住工作中的拥抱并非真正的拥抱，只是其微弱的回响。
如果你在拥抱某人，表现得就像在玩那个叫“手术”的儿童游戏一样。
将手臂环抱对方，但不要实际接触他们身体的任何部位。
让你的脸远离他们的脸：除非对方有异常大的耳垂，否则你绝不应再让自己陷入那种可怕的情形。
